title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated images and videos to impersonate a named, real attorney on social media, creating fake profiles that offered immigration legal services he never provided. The failure here is impersonation: AI tools were used to fabricate a credible professional identity, complete with synthetic video, false client testimonials, and fraudulent contracts, in order to extract money from people seeking immigration help. The scheme operated entirely outside any legitimate deployment, meaning there was no institutional system to audit or constrain it.

The attack surface was the social media platforms themselves. Nearly 6,500 fake profiles accumulated across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before the real attorney's firm hired a third-party anti-piracy company to request their removal. Detection came only after real clients began contacting the attorney's actual office, not through any automated or platform-level safeguard that caught the impersonation before harm occurred.

What is not established is the identity of the scammers, whether any law enforcement action has produced findings, or the total financial loss across all victims.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney, Angel Leal, who has practiced law for over 30 years, is warning the public about criminals using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provided. One fraudulent video offered US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he says the problem has escalated dramatically over the past three months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company to combat the fraud, resulting in the removal of nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The scams typically begin with social media videos directing viewers to contact a phone number through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and payment requests. Other deceptive videos feature false testimonials from supposed clients praising Leal's services. Leal warns consumers to be cautious of anyone requesting payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and emphasizes that his office never requests payments over the phone. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams further.
